title: Bring your own Supabase
description: Imported by OWN-0 from runtime/executive/mission-imports/2026-10-23-customer-ownership.json. Source ticket: OWN-SUPABASE.
objective: A customer moves a project's backend to their own Supabase project: its migrations, edge functions and function secrets are applied there after they read and approve every step, and the app is pointed at it through environment variables.
risks: SQL cannot be undone like a file: a target whose public schema already has tables is refused, each migration runs in its own transaction, and the run stops at the first failure and says how far it got.
The Supabase connection is used only for steps the customer starts; function secrets the customer types are passed to Supabase and never kept by KoreLumina; a service-role key is never recorded.
Data is not moved between projects.
The first live run happens only on the owner's own test Supabase project, with the owner's approval.

tasks.title: Read what the app needs from Supabase
acceptanceCriteria: Lists the environment variables the app reads for Supabase, the migrations in order, the edge functions, and the secrets the functions read

tasks.title: Create a Supabase project on the customer's account
acceptanceCriteria: Creates a new project in the customer's chosen organisation and region through the Management API, or uses an existing empty project
A new project's database password is generated, shown once for the customer to save, and never stored, logged or returned again

tasks.title: Apply migrations, functions and secrets to the customer's project
acceptanceCriteria: Every statement and function is shown before anything runs, and runs only after explicit approval
Refuses a target with existing public tables
Stops at the first failure and reports exactly what ran

tasks.title: Point the app at the new project
acceptanceCriteria: The project URL and anon key go into .env.example and the deployment's environment, never into source code

tasks.title: Supabase window in the Knowledge Operations design
acceptanceCriteria: Shows the plan, real progress and the result
The owner approves it visually and its UI contract is certified
